items.title: Luke Schiro Interview, 1967-12-05
items.q: He played with us a lot

ctx.x: I don't think he was, but he used to sit in the arrogant and all. When you talk about piano players, there's a piano player that I'd like you to hear sometimes. He's a colored fellow. His name is Noel Fusher. He was raised with Lloyd Primm and all of us. Yeah, I don't know him. No, I don't think he did. He had a civil service job. He used to work under me over the port. His uncle played up and he used to call him all this. He used to call Bill Willie. He'd talk about fine kind of thing. It was Bornell Santiago,…
I knew his brother, but I never met him in time. Blackie, I knew him.

Yeah, but this boy was a handsome boy. He could pass the Spanish. He played with us a lot, but then he started to pull up that dope and that was it. He died young, but I don't remember him when he was four years old and playing piano. He couldn't even reach the pedals. He was a little bit of a piano player. They tried to make something out of him. Armstrong came in and heard him. A few of those big bands heard him and all. I don't want to learn how to read. But boy, he had a style.
